trip.name: Patagonia 2026
trip.description: Sixteen days from your home city to the south of Chile and Argentina. Two nights in Santiago and three in Buenos Aires, then a flight to El Calafate. From 26 November the group of 19 travels with Say Hueque: two nights in El Chaltén for Laguna Torre and the Cóndores viewpoints, two in El Calafate for the Perito Moreno Glacier, and four at Hotel Las Torres in Torres del Paine for Base Torres, a park tour with Lago Grey, and the French Valley. The guide ends with the flight from Puerto Natales to Santiago on 4 December.

days.label: Home city to Santiago
days.description: Fly from your home city to Santiago. Most of the group lands at Santiago airport (SCL) on the morning of 20 Nov, and overnight flights are common.
warnings: Solace Hotel asks guests to send arrival details at least 72 hours before arrival. Do this by 17 Nov and ask about early check-in.
Chile's SAG declaration is required for everyone entering Chile, including by air. It can be completed online up to 48 hours before arrival. Do not bring fresh fruit, meat or dairy off the plane.
Indian passport holders: check the entry rules in the Info tab. Chile's exemption depends on holding a US visa valid for at least 6 more months.

days.label: Santiago
days.description:
Land at 07:40 after the overnight flight. Clear immigration (PDI) and the SAG agricultural check, then it is about 30 to 40 minutes by taxi or transfer to Providencia. Check-in at Solace Hotel is from 15:00; ask ahead for early check-in, or leave bags and go out.

Keep the first day easy. Cerro San Cristóbal is close to the hotel: take the funicular up from Bellavista for the view across the city to the Andes, and the cable car down. Barrio Lastarria and the Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes make a relaxed afternoon, and La Chascona, Pablo Neruda's house in Bellavista, is at the foot of the hill. Bellavista and Providencia both have plenty of places for dinner.

options.name: Solace Hotel Santiago
options.address: Monseñor Sotero Sanz 115, Providencia, Santiago, Chile
options.notes: 2 nights. Check-in 15:00, check-out 12:00. Booked under the reservation holder's name. Send arrival details 72 h ahead and ask about early check-in. Paying in foreign currency with a foreign passport and your PDI entry slip exempts the room from Chile's 19% VAT.

days.resupply_notes: Pharmacies, supermarkets and ATMs are easy to find in Providencia. A good day to pick up a local SIM or eSIM if you need one.
warnings: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes and La Chascona are open Tuesday to Sunday, so both are open today and tomorrow.
La Chascona has no advance booking: entry is in order of arrival, with an English audio guide.
La Moneda guided visits run on weekdays only, so today is the only chance. Register in advance on the presidency's visits site and bring your passport.
Pickpocketing is common in crowded parts of central Santiago, on the metro and at café tables. Keep phones and bags in front of you, not on chair backs.

food_stops.name: Galindo
food_stops.notes: Chilean home cooking since 1968, a short walk from La Chascona and the funicular. Pastel de choclo is not vegetarian (beef pino underneath); porotos con riendas can be, but ask for it 'sin longaniza'. Open Fri 12:00-00:00.

food_stops.name: Holy Moly Lastarria
food_stops.notes: Burger bar with several vegetarian and plant-based burgers alongside beef. Easy lunch between Bellas Artes and Cerro Santa Lucía. Open Fri 13:00-00:00.

food_stops.name: Emporio La Rosa
food_stops.notes: Artisan ice cream; try rosa-pistacho or chocolate-albahaca. Sorbet flavours are dairy-free. Open daily 10:00-19:30.

food_stops.name: Bocanáriz
food_stops.notes: Wine bar with a long Chilean list by the glass and themed flights (try a carménère or País flight). Small plates include vegetable dishes; book for evenings. Open Fri 12:30-00:00.

food_stops.name: Peumayén Ancestral Food
food_stops.notes: Tasting boards based on Mapuche, Rapa Nui and Andean cooking, with native breads and ferments. Mostly meat and seafood; ask when booking about a vegetarian board. Open Fri 13:30-23:30, closed Sundays; book.

food_stops.name: El Huerto
food_stops.notes: Santiago's long-running vegetarian restaurant (since 1980), now largely vegan with organic produce. Good for an easy dinner near the hotel; reserve by WhatsApp. Open Mon-Sat 09:00-23:00.

optional_activities.name: Cerro San Cristóbal: funicular up, cable car down
optional_activities.notes: The funicular runs 10:00 to 19:45 Tuesday to Sunday. Tickets online or at the Pío Nono station in Bellavista. Views over the city to the Andes on a clear day.

optional_activities.name: Barrio Lastarria and Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes
optional_activities.notes: A walkable neighbourhood of cafés and small galleries by Cerro Santa Lucía and Parque Forestal. The museum is free, open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 18:30.

optional_activities.name: La Chascona, Pablo Neruda's house
optional_activities.departure: Fernando Márquez de la Plata 0192, Bellavista
optional_activities.notes: Neruda's house in Bellavista at the foot of San Cristóbal. Open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 18:00; no booking, entry in order of arrival. Audio guide in English.

optional_activities.name: Palacio de La Moneda guided visit
optional_activities.notes: Free weekday visits of about 50 minutes; registration required in advance, passport on the day. Visits can be cancelled at short notice.

days.label: Santiago
days.description:
The only full day in Santiago. Two ways to spend it.

In the city: start at Plaza de Armas and walk to the Palacio de La Moneda, with the Museo Chileno de Arte Precolombino in between (allow about 1.5 hours). Have lunch at the Mercado Central, known for seafood, then cross the river to the fruit and vegetable stalls of La Vega Central.

Or out of town: a wine day. The Maipo valley wineries (Concha y Toro, Santa Rita, Cousiño Macul) are under an hour away; Casablanca, known for white wines, is about an hour towards the coast. Book tours ahead.

options.address: Monseñor Sotero Sanz 115, Providencia, Santiago, Chile
options.notes: 2 nights. Check-in 15:00, check-out 12:00. Booked under the reservation holder's name. Send arrival details 72 h ahead and ask about early check-in. Paying in foreign currency with a foreign passport and your PDI entry slip exempts the room from Chile's 19% VAT.

warnings: Museo Chileno de Arte Precolombino is open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 18:00.
Mercado Central is open until about 19:00 on Saturdays; La Vega is busiest and best in the morning.
Winery tours need booking in advance, usually at least a day ahead. Arrange a driver or a tour rather than driving yourself.
Keep valuables out of sight around Plaza de Armas and the markets, which are busy on Saturdays.

food_stops.name: Bar Nacional
food_stops.notes: Old-school fuente de soda a block from the Precolombino museum: sandwiches, cazuela, and a completo italiano (hot dog with tomato, avocado and mayo). Vegetarians: a palta-tomate or cheese sandwich 'sin jamón'. Open Sat until 18:00.

food_stops.name: El Naturista
food_stops.notes: Vegetarian since 1927: soups, legume stews, vegetable tortillas and fresh juices. Here the pastel de choclo is meat-free, unlike elsewhere. Open Sat 09:00-16:00, closed Sun.

food_stops.name: Fuente Alemana
food_stops.area: Centro, Plaza Italia end of the Alameda
food_stops.notes: Counter classic for lomito (slow-cooked pork) and churrasco sandwiches with avocado, tomato and mayo. Little for vegetarians. Open Sat 10:30-21:45, closed Sundays.

food_stops.name: La Piojera
food_stops.notes: Crowded historic cantina two blocks from Mercado Central, known for the terremoto (pipeño wine with pineapple ice cream); one is plenty. Food is meaty; go for the drink. Open Mon-Sat 12:00-20:30.

food_stops.name: Chipe Libre
food_stops.notes: Pisco bar with 100+ Chilean and Peruvian piscos; order a pisco sour or a tasting. Bar snacks include vegetable options. Open Sat 13:00-01:00, closed Sundays.

optional_activities.name: Historic centre and Museo Chileno de Arte Precolombino
optional_activities.notes: Plaza de Armas, the cathedral and the museum one block away (Bandera 361), with pre-Columbian art from across the Americas. Allow about 1.5 hours inside.

optional_activities.name: Mercado Central and La Vega Central
optional_activities.notes: Seafood lunch in the 1872 iron market hall, then across the Mapocho to the produce market.

optional_activities.name: Maipo valley wineries
optional_activities.operator: Concha y Toro / Santa Rita / Cousiño Macul
optional_activities.notes: An alternative full day. Concha y Toro (Pirque) and Santa Rita (Alto Jahuel) are under an hour from the city; Cousiño Macul is inside Santiago, in Peñalolén. All need booking.

optional_activities.name: Casablanca valley
optional_activities.notes: About 80 km towards the coast on Route 68, known for cool-climate white wines. Go with a driver or a tour; wineries need booking.

days.label: Santiago to Buenos Aires
days.description:
Leave the hotel around 09:00 for the airport (check-out is by 12:00). LATAM LA 455 leaves Santiago at 11:28 and lands at Buenos Aires Aeroparque (AEP) at 14:40. Aeroparque is in the city, a short taxi ride from Palermo.

The hotel is Miravida Soho in Palermo Soho; check-in from 15:00. Spend the evening in the neighbourhood: small shops, cafés and parrillas within a few blocks. The San Telmo Sunday fair on Calle Defensa is possible if you have the energy, but with a 14:40 landing it is tight. San Telmo is worth a visit on any day.

flights.notes: Recheck the time in the LATAM app. Published schedules put this flight at about 12:30 while Chile is on summer time, so it may leave about an hour later than booked; arrival 14:40 is unchanged.

options.name: Miravida Soho Hotel & Wine Bar
options.notes: 3 nights. Check-in 15:00, check-out 11:00. The reservation holder must show the booking card and matching photo ID at check-in. A small city tax is charged per person per night.

warnings: Recheck the LA 455 times in the LATAM app before travel. Other flights on this trip were re-timed after Chile's summer-time change; no change has been seen for this one.
Miravida requires the card used for the booking and a matching photo ID at check-in. The reservation holder must be present.
Room VAT: paying with a non-Argentine card and showing a foreign passport and your Argentine entry record exempts the room from Argentina's 21% VAT. Keep the entry record.
Indian passport holders: Argentina now admits Indian nationals holding a valid US visa without an Argentine visa or AVE. See the Info tab.

food_stops.name: El Huerto (breakfast)
food_stops.notes: Same place as the Day 2 dinner suggestion; one of the few kitchens near the hotel open early on Sunday. Vegan brunch plate with black bean tacos. Open Sun 09:00-16:00.

food_stops.name: Colmado Coffee & Bakery
food_stops.notes: Sourdough, cakes and good coffee, about 10 minutes by taxi from the hotel. Sunday hours reported as 10:00-21:00; busy, arrive early.

food_stops.name: Parrilla Don Julio
food_stops.notes: The best-known parrilla in the city, a few blocks from the hotel; book online weeks ahead. Vegetarians: provoleta (grilled provolone), grilled vegetables, salads. Open daily 19:00-01:00.

food_stops.name: Ninina (Borges)
food_stops.notes: Bakery-café near the hotel for coffee and medialunas after the flight, or a light early supper. The Gorriti branch opens 09:00-21:00 on weekends; this branch's hours are not listed.

optional_activities.name: Palermo Soho evening
optional_activities.notes: The hotel's neighbourhood. Shops, cafés and parrillas around Plaza Serrano.

optional_activities.name: Feria de San Telmo
optional_activities.notes: Sunday street fair on Calle Defensa around Plaza Dorrego, 10:00 to 17:00. With a 14:40 landing, you would have about an hour. Optional.

days.label: Buenos Aires
days.description:
Monday 23 November is a national holiday in Argentina (Día de la Soberanía Nacional, moved from Friday 20th), so the city is on a long weekend: expect more people at the sights and some shops closed.

Spend the morning in Recoleta: the cemetery, with its mausoleums including Eva Perón's family tomb, and the streets and cafés around it. MALBA, the museum of Latin American art, is a short walk or taxi ride away and is open today (it closes on Tuesdays). Casa Rosada runs free guided visits on weekends and public holidays, so today may be possible; book online up to 15 days ahead.

In the evening, tango: a traditional milonga such as La Catedral or El Beso, or a dinner show.

options.name: Miravida Soho Hotel & Wine Bar
options.notes: 3 nights. Check-in 15:00, check-out 11:00. The reservation holder must show the booking card and matching photo ID at check-in. A small city tax is charged per person per night.

warnings: Public holiday: check opening times the day before. The Rosedal and the Museo Casa Rosada are closed on Mondays.
Recoleta Cemetery charges foreign visitors an entrance fee, payable by card only. Hours are about 09:00 to 17:00.
Casa Rosada visits need advance booking (opens about 15 days ahead) and a passport on the day.
Pickpocketing and bag snatching happen in busy areas, on the subway and at café tables. Keep phones in hand or zipped away, and bags on your lap.

food_stops.name: La Biela
food_stops.notes: Classic café by the Recoleta cemetery; café con leche and medialunas under the big rubber tree. Open daily 08:00-01:00.

food_stops.name: El Sanjuanino
food_stops.notes: Small, long-running empanada and locro spot near the cemetery. Vegetarians: empanadas de humita (sweetcorn) or queso; locro contains pork and beef.

food_stops.name: Coronado (at MALBA)
food_stops.notes: The museum's restaurant: Argentine cooking with seasonal produce, a coffee bar and a terrace. Handy before or after the galleries. Open Mon-Fri 08:00-01:00; book via coronado.meitre.com.

food_stops.name: Chuí
food_stops.notes: Wood-fired, vegetable-led cooking in a large garden space, vegan dishes marked on the menu. The vegetarian alternative to a parrilla night. Monday 19:00-00:00; book by WhatsApp.

food_stops.name: La Cabrera
food_stops.notes: Big-portion parrilla, easier to book than Don Julio; 40% off 18:30-20:00 daily. Vegetarians: provoleta and the small side dishes that come with mains. Open daily 12:00-16:00 and 18:30-01:00.

food_stops.name: Florería Atlántico
food_stops.notes: Cocktail bar behind a flower shop, a regular on world bar lists. Book by email or WhatsApp. Monday and holiday opening not shown online.

optional_activities.name: Recoleta Cemetery
optional_activities.notes: Ornate family mausoleums, including the Duarte family tomb where Eva Perón is buried. Entry fee for foreign visitors, card only. Junín 1760.

optional_activities.name: MALBA
optional_activities.notes: Latin American art from the 20th century to today. Open Wednesday 11:00 to 20:00 and Thursday to Monday 12:00 to 20:00; closed Tuesdays. Tickets online.

optional_activities.name: Casa Rosada guided visit
optional_activities.notes: Free visits on weekends and public holidays. Book online, up to 15 days ahead; bring your passport and arrive 20 minutes early.

optional_activities.name: Tango: a milonga or a show
optional_activities.notes: A milonga is a social dance evening, the local version. La Catedral (Almagro) and El Beso (Riobamba 416) are long-running. A dinner show is more polished.

days.label: Buenos Aires
days.description:
The historic centre and the south of the city. Start at Plaza de Mayo, with the Casa Rosada, the Cabildo and the Metropolitan Cathedral around it, then walk down Avenida de Mayo to Café Tortoni, the city's oldest café.

In the afternoon take a taxi to La Boca to see Caminito, the short street of painted tenement houses near the old port. Go in daylight and stay in the main tourist area. San Telmo, between the centre and La Boca, is worth a walk for its old streets and antique shops even without the Sunday fair.

Parrilla dinner tonight if you did not go yesterday.

options.name: Miravida Soho Hotel & Wine Bar
options.notes: 3 nights. Check-in 15:00, check-out 11:00. The reservation holder must show the booking card and matching photo ID at check-in. A small city tax is charged per person per night.

warnings: MALBA is closed on Tuesdays.
La Boca: visit in daytime and stay around Caminito. Use a taxi or ride-hailing app to get there and back rather than walking in from other areas.
Watch bags and phones on Florida Street and around Plaza de Mayo, where pickpockets and phone snatchers work the crowds.

food_stops.name: Café La Puerto Rico
food_stops.notes: Historic café two blocks from Plaza de Mayo that roasts its own coffee; a quieter alternative to Tortoni. Medialunas and tostados (ask 'sin jamón').

food_stops.name: Bar El Federal
food_stops.notes: Old corner bar with a carved wooden counter; sandwiches, tartas and milanesas, and a good spot for a vermouth. Vegetarians: tarta de verdura, or revuelto gramajo without ham.

food_stops.name: El Cuartito
food_stops.notes: Pizzeria since 1934; eat standing at the counter. Order fugazzeta (onion and mozzarella) or muzzarella with a slice of fainá, all vegetarian. Open Tue-Sun 12:30-00:30.

food_stops.name: La Brigada
food_stops.notes: San Telmo parrilla since 1992, football shirts on the walls; the waiters cut the steak with a spoon. Vegetarians: provoleta, grilled vegetables, salads. Reserve by phone or WhatsApp.

optional_activities.name: Plaza de Mayo and Avenida de Mayo
optional_activities.notes: Casa Rosada, the Cabildo and the cathedral, then Café Tortoni (open daily 08:00 to 21:00, Av. de Mayo 825).

optional_activities.name: La Boca and Caminito
optional_activities.notes: Painted houses, street tango and craft stalls. Daytime only; the city runs a tourist help point there.

optional_activities.name: San Telmo
optional_activities.notes: Cobbled streets, antique shops and Plaza Dorrego, on the way between the centre and La Boca.

days.label: Buenos Aires to El Calafate
days.description:
A morning walk in the Bosques de Palermo and the Rosedal rose garden, close to the hotel, then check out by 11:00. Aerolíneas Argentinas AR 1852 leaves Aeroparque at 14:20 and lands in El Calafate at 17:40, a flight of about 3 h 20 m.

El Calafate airport is about 20 km east of town. Take a taxi or remis from the rank outside arrivals to the Calafate Parque Hotel, about 20 to 25 minutes. Tonight is not part of the Say Hueque booking; tomorrow's transfer to El Chaltén collects you from this hotel.

If the booking is confirmed, the evening is a sunset kayak on Lago Argentino. It depends on landing on time and a quick hotel drop-off.

transport_after_hike.notes: Taxis wait outside arrivals. Fixed fares are usual; confirm before you set off.

taxi_services.name: Taxi Cóndor (airport concession)
taxi_services.notes: Counter in the arrivals hall. Also +54 2902 491655.

taxi_services.name: Taxi Remis Calafate
taxi_services.notes: Book ahead for a pick-up at the airport.

taxi_services.name: VES Patagonia shuttle
taxi_services.notes: Shared shuttle, counter in arrivals. Slower than a taxi.

options.name: Calafate Parque Hotel
options.address: Gobernador Gregores esq. 7 de Diciembre, El Calafate
options.notes: 1 night, 25 Nov. Not part of the Say Hueque booking. The listed phone is the hotel group's line; the hotel also takes WhatsApp on +54 9 2235 047993.

days.resupply_notes: El Calafate's main street, Av. del Libertador, has supermarkets, pharmacies and ATMs. A good evening to take out Argentine pesos for El Chaltén.
warnings: Check-out at Miravida is 11:00 and the flight leaves AEP at 14:20. Aeroparque is about 20 minutes from Palermo in normal traffic; aim to be there by 12:30.
The kayak depends on landing on time. If the flight is late, the operator may move or cancel it.
Nights in El Calafate are cold even in late November. Keep a warm layer in your hand luggage.

food_stops.name: Ninina (Gorriti)
food_stops.notes: Bakery-café for a proper breakfast: pastries, toast, eggs and good coffee. Close to the hotel; allow an hour. Open Mon-Fri 08:00-21:00.

food_stops.name: Cuervo Café (Soho)
food_stops.notes: Specialty coffee roaster; a flat white and pastry on the way to the Rosedal. Open Tue-Sun 08:00-20:00.

food_stops.name: Buenos Aires Verde
food_stops.notes: Vegetarian café-restaurant with bowls, wraps, juices and raw desserts. Order to take away for the flight if time is tight.

food_stops.name: Ninina (Borges)
food_stops.notes: Closest option to the hotel for pastries or a sandwich to take to Aeroparque (ask 'sin jamón').

food_stops.name: Pura Vida
food_stops.area: El Calafate (west end of the main street)
food_stops.notes: Homemade stews, soups and bread in a colourful, relaxed room. Vegetarian section on the menu; vegan lentil and potato pie, pumpkin soup. For meat eaters: cazuela de cordero (lamb stew). Group: Popular and not large. Phone ahead for 19 (+54 2902 493356) and expect split tables.

food_stops.name: Isabel Cocina al Disco
food_stops.notes: Dishes cooked on the disco (a wide steel pan over a fire). Vegetarian and vegan discos as well as lamb and guanaco; takes care with coeliac requests. Group: Takes reservations (reservas.calafate@isabelcocinaaldisco.com, WhatsApp +54 9 2966 707320) and welcomes large groups. Book early.

food_stops.name: La Tablita
food_stops.area: El Calafate (across the stream from the centre)
food_stops.notes: The town's oldest parrilla (1968): Patagonian lamb on the asador. Veg: provoleta (grilled cheese), grilled vegetables, salads, pasta, empanadas de queso; order veg sides as a main. Group: Takes reservations (+54 2902 49-1065); the large dining room suits 19. Book a day or two ahead.

food_stops.name: La Lechuzita
food_stops.notes: Pizzeria and an easy group option: pizza, empanadas, pasta. Veg: pizza de verduras, fugazzeta (cheese and onion), empanadas de humita. Group: Phone ahead (02902 491-620) for 19.

food_stops.name: La Zorra Taproom
food_stops.notes: The local brewery's taproom, with bar snacks. Ask whether a calafate-berry beer is on tap; Calafate Sour cocktails are served in bars around town. Group: Busy after 21:00. For 19, arrive early or message ahead.

food_stops.name: Heladería Acuarela (calafate ice cream)
food_stops.notes: Try calafate-berry ice cream, a little like blueberry. Water-based fruit flavours are usually vegan; ask. Helados Tito is the locals' alternative.

optional_activities.name: Sunset kayak on Lago Argentino
optional_activities.notes: Moved from 29 Nov; booking to be confirmed. The flight lands at 17:40 and sunset is about 21:30, so confirm a start time that allows for the airport and hotel. Some listings show an 18:00 start, which would be too early. Bring a dry change of clothes.

optional_activities.name: Bosques de Palermo and the Rosedal
optional_activities.notes: The rose garden in Parque Tres de Febrero, near the hotel, in bloom in late spring. Open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 18:00.

days.label: El Calafate to El Chaltén
days.description:
Say Hueque's private transfer takes you north from El Calafate to El Chaltén, about 215 km and 3 hours on paved road. The route crosses open steppe along Lago Argentino, then follows Ruta 40 past La Leona, a roadhouse dating from the 1890s, and along the shore of Lago Viedma. On a clear day the Fitz Roy massif is visible well before you reach town.

El Chaltén is a small village at the northern edge of Los Glaciares National Park and the start point for tomorrow's walk. Use the afternoon to walk around town, stop at the park visitor centre at the entrance to the village for the trail and weather briefing, and buy tomorrow's lunch: the Laguna Torre trek does not include a box lunch.

transport_to_start.time: Time to be confirmed by Say Hueque
transport_to_start.notes: The Say Hueque booking starts from your El Calafate hotel. Tell Say Hueque which hotel you stayed in on 25 Nov.

options.name: Desierto Suites
options.address: Pasaje Iñaki Coussirat 88, El Chaltén (9301), Santa Cruz
options.notes: 2 nights, 26-28 Nov. Breakfast included. Booked by Say Hueque.

days.resupply_notes: El Chaltén has small supermarkets, bakeries and delis. Buy lunch and snacks for tomorrow's trek this evening. Bring enough cash from El Calafate; ATMs in El Chaltén can run out.
warnings: The transfer time is not yet confirmed. Say Hueque will send it before the trip.
Tomorrow's box lunch is not included. Buy it this evening; shops may not be open before the 08:30 pick-up.

waypoints.note: Hotel pick-up by the Say Hueque driver

waypoints.name: La Leona
waypoints.note: Historic roadhouse on Ruta 40, roughly halfway. Ask the driver if a short stop is possible.

waypoints.name: El Chaltén
waypoints.note: About 3 hours and 215 km from El Calafate

food_stops.name: Parador La Leona
food_stops.area: Ruta 40, about 110 km from El Calafate (halfway to El Chaltén)
food_stops.notes: Historic roadhouse from 1894 by the La Leona river. Coffee, homemade cakes, sandwiches and empanadas. Veg: empanadas de queso or verdura, cakes. Group: Groups are routine, but tables fill when tour buses stop. Order quickly.

food_stops.name: Cúrcuma
food_stops.notes: Fully vegan. Easy late lunch on arrival (wraps, pizza, burgers, juices). Order day 9 vegan trail boxes here at the same time. Group: Small room. For more than 6-8 people, message on Instagram a day ahead; order trail boxes the afternoon before.

food_stops.name: Lo de Haydee (bakery)
food_stops.notes: Bread, facturas (pastries) and sandwiches. Sandwiches default to jamón y queso; ask for 'vegetariano' or 'sin jamón' (queso y tomate, verduras). Group: For 19 box lunches, order the afternoon before with a count of veg and vegan.

food_stops.name: Che Empanadas
food_stops.notes: Empanadas travel well in a daypack and are fine cold. Veg fillings to ask for: verdura (chard/spinach), queso y cebolla, humita (sweetcorn), caprese. Buy the evening before. Group: Order 40-60 empanadas a day ahead for the group.

food_stops.name: Puentes Amarillos Tienda Natural
food_stops.notes: Health-food shop. Makes vegan box lunches for hikers (vegan 'ham and cheese' sandwiches, vegan alfajores); also tofu, hummus, nuts, dried fruit, bars. Group: Order boxes the afternoon before.

food_stops.name: La Senyera
food_stops.notes: Family-run, in an old wool-shearing shed. About half the menu is vegetarian, with around five vegan plates (falafel, burgers, stews, salad); vegan locro reported. One of the more affordable places in town. Group: Ask whether they can take the whole group; book a day ahead.

food_stops.name: La Tapera
food_stops.notes: Long-running Patagonian dinner spot: lamb, stews, homemade pasta. Cordero patagónico is lamb. Veg: pastas caseras (ask for a sauce without meat), provoleta, vegetable soup, salads. Group: Takes reservations (+54 2962 49-3195). Book well ahead for 19; the room is small, so expect two tables or two sittings.

food_stops.name: La Cervecería Chaltén (brew pub)
food_stops.notes: The town's original brew pub, in a wooden cabin: pilsner, bock, weissbier, amber. Known for locro (a stew, usually with meat) and pizza. Veg: pizza, empanadas de verdura or queso; ask whether there is a vegetable locro. Group: Small and busy after hiking. For the full group, go before 19:00 or split across two bars.

days.description:
A full-day walk with a private English-speaking guide (Walk Patagonia) to Laguna Torre, the glacial lake at the foot of Cerro Torre. The guide meets you at the hotel at 08:30. The route is an out-and-back on the same path. Say Hueque lists it as 19 km, 7 to 8 hours, moderate, with a high point of 719 m; the figures shown here come from the route file.

The trail leaves from the western edge of the village and follows the Fitz Roy River. After about 20 minutes you reach the river canyon and its waterfalls. Most of the climbing is in the first 2 km. The first viewpoint looks at Cerro Torre, its glaciers and the Adela range; if anyone wants a shorter day, this is the turn-back point, about 3 hours round trip from town. Beyond it the path runs mostly level through lenga woodland and meadows to the De Agostini camp and then over moraine to the lake, where ice from Glaciar Grande floats below Cerro Torre. Lunch is at the lake, then back the same way.

Cerro Torre is often in cloud by midday, so the early start helps. Mirador Maestri, a ridge viewpoint about 20 minutes beyond the lake, is possible if the guide judges there is time and the weather allows.

days.description:
A short guided walk to two viewpoints above El Chaltén, then the drive back to El Calafate. The guide (Walk Patagonia, private, English-speaking) meets you at 09:00 at the hotel or an agreed meeting point. Say Hueque lists it as 6.99 km with 183 m of climbing, 2 to 3 hours; the figures shown here are from the route file and depend on where you start and finish.

From the bridge over the Fitz Roy River at the entrance to town the path passes the park offices and climbs for about 40 minutes to Mirador de los Cóndores. It looks back over the village to Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre and down the Río de las Vueltas valley; condors are often seen here. About 30 minutes further, Mirador de las Águilas faces the other way, over the steppe to Lago Viedma. The guide leaves you at the end of the walk and you walk back to the hotel on your own.

In the afternoon a private transfer takes you back to El Calafate, about 200 km and 3 hours.

days.description:
A full day at the Perito Moreno Glacier with a private English-speaking guide (Huellas del Sur). Hotel pick-up is at 08:00 for the 80 km drive into Los Glaciares National Park; the park entrance and the boat ticket are included.

The boat leaves at 10:00 from the Bajo las Sombras port, 7 km before the walkways. The one-hour Nautical Safari runs along Brazo Rico beside the south face of the glacier, which stands 60 to 70 m above the water. A bus then takes you up to the walkways on the Magallanes peninsula. After the guide's briefing at the main balcony you have free time on the circuits, which drop in stages towards the lake and look straight across the channel at the glacier's front. Ice falling from the face is common through the day. Return to El Calafate at the meeting time set by the guide. Allow 7 to 8 hours in total.

Lunch is not included. There is a restaurant and a café at the walkways, or bring food from town. The boat runs subject to weather.

days.description:
A private transfer, booked through Hotel Las Torres, takes you from El Calafate across the border into Chile and on to Torres del Paine: about 275 km and 4 hours, plus time at the two border posts. The drive is almost all open steppe. You clear Argentine exit formalities, then Chilean immigration and the SAG agricultural check.

Before you go: every traveller must complete Chile's SAG digital affidavit on their phone within 48 hours before crossing, and have their passport to hand. Do not carry fresh fruit, vegetables, meat, dairy, plants or seeds. Eat or leave them in El Calafate. If unsure about anything, declare it.

Hotel Las Torres sits on an estancia at the foot of the Ascencio valley, where the Base Torres trail starts. Staff give an arrival briefing and explain the excursion list. Depending on when you arrive, you can join a half-day activity. From tonight all meals, the open bar and park excursions are included, as is the Torres del Paine park entrance.

days.description:
Excursions at Las Torres are chosen on site each evening from the hotel's list. The recommended one for today is the trek to the Base Torres viewpoint, and it starts at the hotel door. It is about 19 km round trip with about 975 m of climbing. Las Torres rates it high difficulty and allows about 8 hours; plan on 8 to 9.

The path crosses the Ascencio River and climbs the hillside to the Windy Pass, where the valley opens. It then contours along the Ascencio valley and drops to Refugio Chileno (about km 5.5), continues through lenga forest to the Torres camp, and ends with the hardest part: La Morrena, a steep climb of about 45 to 60 minutes over loose boulders, to the lake below the three granite towers. After a snack and photos you return the same way.

The towers are often in cloud. The guide will watch the forecast; if the top is clouded in, turning at Chileno or the forest is still a good day.

The recommended excursion today is Full Paine with Lago Grey, a road trip through the park with short walks at each stop. It is an easier day between the two long treks. Las Torres rates it easy and lists 7 to 10 hours; walking adds up to about 9 km.

Stops include Puente Negro, the Nordenskjöld and Sarmiento viewpoints, Lago Pehoé and the Salto Grande waterfall between Lago Nordenskjöld and Lago Pehoé. After lunch you choose between two ways to see Grey Glacier: a walk along the south shore of Lago Grey to a point looking over the floating ice, or a boat up the lake to the glacier front.

days.description:
The recommended excursion for the last full day is the French Valley, the middle arm of the W Trek. It is a long day: Las Torres lists 12 hours door to door, high difficulty, with 700 to 800 m of height change; about 10 hours of that is walking. The transfer and the Pehoé boat are included.

After a 45-minute drive to Pudeto you take the Hielos Patagónicos catamaran across Lago Pehoé (about 30 minutes) to Paine Grande. The first part of the trail is gently rolling along the north side of Lago Skottsberg to the Italiano camp at the mouth of the valley, where there is a break for water and snacks. You can turn back here. The rest continue for about 2.5 km up a steep path through lenga forest and then rock, to a viewpoint below Los Cuernos looking at the French Glacier on the side of Cerro Paine Grande and back down the valley to the lakes. Then back the same way to catch the return boat.

The boat times are fixed, so the guide sets a turnaround time. Keep a steady pace and eat regularly.

weather.description:
Late spring in both countries. Santiago is warm and dry: about 27 °C by day and 10 °C at night in late November. Buenos Aires is warm and more humid, about 26 °C by day and 16 °C at night, with the chance of a thunderstorm.

Patagonia is much cooler. El Calafate averages about 16 °C by day and 4 °C at night in November, a little warmer in December; El Chaltén is similar. Torres del Paine is cooler and windier, often around 10 °C by day and close to freezing at night, and November is its windiest month. Days are long: in El Calafate the sun rises around 05:35 and sets around 21:35 in early December, about 16 hours of daylight. Wind is what defines the weather here: steady wind of 30 to 50 km/h is normal and gusts at passes and viewpoints can go well above that. Rain, sleet and sunshine can all arrive within an hour, so pack layers and carry them every day.
alerts: Wind is the main hazard on the trails. In strong gusts, stop, crouch and wait.
UV is high in southern Patagonia in spring. Use SPF 50 and sunglasses even when it feels cold.
Carry waterproof layers every day, whatever the morning looks like.
Snow is possible on higher ground in Torres del Paine in early December.
Santiago and Buenos Aires can be hot at midday. Carry water on the city days.

preparation.overview: The first week is city time: walking around Santiago and Buenos Aires, with long days on your feet but no hills to speak of. The hiking is in the second half: six walking days in nine, three of them long. The hardest are Laguna Torre (day 9), Base Torres (day 13) and the French Valley (day 15). None are back to back: easier days fall between them. The walking is not technical, but Patagonian wind and changeable weather make every day harder than the numbers suggest.

what_to_expect: Day 1: Travel day. Flight from your home city to Santiago, often overnight. Sleep where you can.
Day 2: Arrive in Santiago; most flights land in the morning. Keep the day light: a walk up or a ride up San Cristóbal and a quiet afternoon.
Day 3: Full day in Santiago. A lot of city walking, or a relaxed wine day.
Day 4: Midday flight to Buenos Aires, landing mid-afternoon. An easy evening in Palermo.
Day 5: Public holiday in Buenos Aires. Recoleta and MALBA on foot; a late night if you go to a milonga.
Day 6: Historic centre and La Boca. Plenty of walking on pavements; taxis between areas.
Day 7: Morning walk, then the afternoon flight to El Calafate. Possible evening kayak, which needs light paddling effort only.
Day 8: Three-hour drive to El Chaltén. Rest your legs and buy tomorrow's lunch.
Day 9: Laguna Torre (about 17 km, 530 m of climbing, 7-8 hours). The first 3 km climb steadily; after that the path rolls and rises gently to the lake. A full, steady day.
Day 10: Cóndores and Águilas (about 7 km, 240 m). Short and over quickly, then a three-hour drive.
Day 11: Perito Moreno. The boat and walkways are gentle, but there are many stairs on the lower circuits and it is cold next to the ice.
Day 12: Long transfer to Torres del Paine with a border crossing. A rest day for the legs.

Day 13: Base Torres (about 19 km, 975 m, 8-9 hours). The hardest day. A steep climb to the Windy Pass early on (about 300 m in 2 km), forest walking past Chileno, then a steep, loose boulder slope for the last 45-60 minutes. Expect tired legs.
Day 14: Full Paine and Lago Grey (about 9 km of short walks). An easier day in the van between the two long treks.
Day 15: French Valley (about 19 km, 690 m, 12 hours door to door). Long rather than steep until the last 2.5 km. The boat times set the pace.
Day 16: Early transfer to Puerto Natales and the 12:00 flight to Santiago. No physical demands.

general_info.visa_info: US passports. Argentina: no visa for tourist stays up to 90 days and no reciprocity fee (Argentine Embassy in the US). Chile: no visa for tourist stays up to 90 days and no fee (Chilean Ministry of Foreign Affairs). Indian passports. Argentina: since 28 August 2025, Indian nationals holding a valid US visa may enter as tourists for up to 90 days without an Argentine visa or the AVE electronic travel authorisation (Resolución 353/2025, Boletín Oficial, 27 Aug 2025). A US B1/B2 or B2 visitor visa is the clear case; carry it in the passport. Without a qualifying US visa you need an Argentine visa or an AVE, which can take up to 20 business days: https://www.migraciones.gob.ar/ave/ Chile: Indian nationals holding a US visa of any type except C (transit), valid for at least 6 months on arrival, do not need a Chilean visa for tourist stays up to 90 days (Embassy of Chile in India). This trip enters Chile on 20 Nov and again on 30 Nov, so the US visa should be valid until at least early June 2027. Both countries are entered twice: Chile on 20 Nov (Santiago airport) and 30 Nov (by road); Argentina on 22 Nov (Aeroparque); the 25 Nov flight to El Calafate is domestic. Chile records entry electronically; keep the PDI slip you are given, as hotels ask for it for the VAT exemption. Rules change: confirm before you travel at https://www.boletinoficial.gob.ar/detalleAviso/primera/330397/20250827 and https://www.chile.gob.cl/nueva-delhi/visas/visas
general_info.health_insurance: Travel insurance with medical evacuation cover is essential. The trekking areas are remote; the nearest well-equipped hospitals are in El Calafate and Punta Arenas, and evacuation is expensive without cover. Check that the policy covers guided day hiking and, if you do the kayak on 25 Nov, kayaking. Carry the policy number and the insurer's 24-hour emergency line on your phone and on paper.

general_info.currency: Argentina uses the Argentine peso (ARS). Foreign Visa and Mastercard cards are charged at a rate linked to the dólar MEP, a market rate, and in 2026 this is close to what cash dollars fetch, so paying by card is usually simplest. Avoid ATM withdrawals, which carry high fees and low limits. Carry some clean US dollar notes as a backup. Hotel VAT: paying for the room with a foreign-issued card and showing a foreign passport exempts it from the 21% VAT; paying cash does not qualify (AFIP/ARCA rules for foreign tourists). Chile uses the Chilean peso (CLP); cards work almost everywhere in Santiago. Hotel VAT: foreign tourists who pay in foreign currency, or with a foreign card charged in US dollars, and show their passport and PDI entry slip are exempt from the 19% VAT (SII). Park fees: Los Glaciares for El Chaltén is not included (buy online, see day 9); Perito Moreno is included; Torres del Paine is included through Las Torres. Tipping: about 10% in restaurants in both countries; a tip for guides and drivers is customary.
general_info.language: Spanish in both countries, with noticeably different accents. English is spoken at the hotels and by the guides. Useful phrases: '¿Cuánto cuesta?' (How much is it?), 'La cuenta, por favor' (The bill, please), '¿Dónde está...?' (Where is...?), 'No hablo español' (I don't speak Spanish).
general_info.mobile_coverage: Santiago and Buenos Aires: good 4G. El Chaltén: patchy 4G in town, none on the trails. El Calafate: good in town, none at the glacier. Torres del Paine: little or no signal; Hotel Las Torres has Wi-Fi for guests. You need mobile data for the SAG declaration (within 48 h before each Chile entry) and the airline apps, so set up an eSIM that covers both countries, or buy local SIMs. Download offline maps before the trip.

general_info.additional_notes: Time zones: in late November and December Santiago (Chile summer time), Magallanes including Torres del Paine, and Argentina are all UTC-3. No clock changes during the trip. Power: 220 V in both countries. Chile uses type C and L plugs; Argentina type I, with type C also common. Biosecurity: Chile's SAG rules apply at every entry. Complete the digital declaration (https://djsimple.sag.gob.cl/) within 48 hours before arriving, and do not bring fresh fruit, vegetables, meat, dairy, honey, plants or seeds; declare anything you are unsure of. Operator: days 8-16 are arranged by Say Hueque; the Torres del Paine days are Hotel Las Torres' own programme, and excursions are chosen on site each evening.

food_tips.Santiago: Say 'soy vegetariano/a, no como carne, pollo, jamón ni pescado'. Pastel de choclo, empanadas de pino, cazuela and porotos granados often contain beef, chicken or pork (porotos may have longaniza); humitas and empanadas de queso are usually safe. Soups and legume dishes are often made with meat stock, so ask 'sin caldo de carne'. For sandwiches, palta-tomate-queso is safe; a Barros Jarpa has ham, so ask 'sin jamón'.
food_tips.Buenos Aires: Say 'soy vegetariano/a, sin carne, pollo ni jamón'. At a parrilla, order provoleta, grilled vegetables (verduras a la parrilla), papas fritas and salads. Empanadas de humita, queso y cebolla, or verdura are the vegetarian ones; locro contains pork and beef. Watch for jamón in tostados, tartas, 'ensalada completa', revuelto gramajo and pizza especial. Pizza fugazzeta and muzzarella are safe. Dinner starts late, 21:00 is normal; book parrillas ahead.
food_tips.El Chaltén: A small village: almost everything is on or within two blocks of Av. San Martín. Many restaurants and bars are seasonal (roughly Oct-Apr) and late November is early season, so most are open but some keep short hours or close one day a week; check Instagram the week before. Dinner from about 19:30; locals eat after 21:00. With 19 people, book dinner every night and expect to split across two tables or two restaurants; small places (Laborum, Cúrcuma, Lo del Manu) cannot seat the whole group. The Laguna Torre lunch (day 9) is not included and nothing is sold on the trail: order box lunches on the afternoon of day 8 (Cúrcuma for vegan boxes, Puentes Amarillos, the bakeries) or buy empanadas and supermarket food that evening. Sandwiches default to jamón y queso; ask for 'vegetariano' or 'sin jamón'. Veg at traditional places: empanadas de verdura, queso y cebolla or humita; provoleta; pizza; pastas caseras with tomato or cream sauce. Ask whether the locro has meat; it usually does. Cordero patagónico is lamb. Craft beer is the local drink: La Cervecería, La Zorra, Don Guerra (San Martín 580), Bourbon (San Martín 401), Cayetano (San Martín 84). Carry cash: some places have been reported as cash-only, and card terminals and signal can be patchy.
food_tips.El Calafate: Restaurants, bakeries and the La Anónima supermarket sit along Av. del Libertador and the streets just off it; both hotels are within walking distance. Dinner from about 19:30-20:00. For 19 people, book dinner a day or two ahead: La Tablita and Isabel Cocina al Disco take groups, and Isabel has vegetarian and vegan discos (closed Tuesdays; days 7, 10 and 11 are Wed, Sat and Sun). Pura Vida and Viva la Pepa are the easiest vegetarian and vegan choices. At a parrilla, vegetarians can order provoleta, grilled vegetables, salads and pasta. Try calafate-berry ice cream, a Calafate Sour, or calafate jam. For Perito Moreno (day 11), a picnic from La Anónima or a bakery bought the evening before costs much less than the walkways restaurant. Calafate Coffee Roasters is closed on Sundays. Before the Chile crossing (day 12): finish or leave all fresh fruit, vegetables, meat, dairy, cheese and homemade sandwiches in El Calafate. Sealed packaged snacks are usually allowed, but declare all food on the SAG form.
food_tips.Hotel Las Torres: Las Torres caters for vegetarians as standard. Coirón's official page says there are 'exquisite options for vegetarians and meat eaters', and the box lunch has a vegetarian sandwich. Vegan and allergy menus are not published. Tell Say Hueque at booking so the request goes into the Las Torres reservation. Las Torres takes 'special requests' at booking by email or WhatsApp. Confirm again at check-in and at each evening excursion briefing, when box lunches are ordered. Expect: an à la carte dinner at Coirón with at least one vegetarian main (vegan by adapting it), a breakfast buffet with fruit, bread and eggs, and the vegetarian box-lunch sandwich (without cheese for vegans). Vegans should bring backup trail snacks. Evidence: lastorres.com Coirón page (27 Sep 2026); Going Awesome Places review (Aug 2025). No published Las Torres dietary policy was found (the help-centre URL returns 404).
food_tips.Refugios on the trails: 2026-27 operators: Chileno (and Central and Cuernos) are run by Las Torres Patagonia, the former Fantástico Sur brand, which is still listed as fslodges.com on some directories. Paine Grande (and Grey, Dickson and Los Perros) are run by Vértice Patagonia, which has 2026-27 commercial terms published. Italiano is a CONAF ranger camp with nothing for sale. Refugios sell snacks, hot drinks, beer, and burgers, pizza and quesadillas. Vegetarian à la carte items are limited (cheese quesadilla, veggie pizza, sandwiches). Pre-booked set meals come in regular and vegetarian versions, with vegan choices limited. Cards are generally accepted, but carry some CLP cash in case the connection is down. Prices are not published for 2026-27. Guide figures from 2023: sandwich CLP 5,000, burger CLP 13,000, beer CLP 6,000 to 8,000.
food_tips.Las Torres open bar: Included: 'Open bar, except premium beer, wine, and spirits' (lastorres.com all-inclusive page, 27 Sep 2026). In practice, calafate sour, pisco sour, house cocktails, carménère and other house wines, and the Pionera house beer are included. Only a few items are marked premium on the Bar Pionero menu (certain whiskies, vodkas, piscos and wines); those are charged, as are tips and laundry. Meals at the bar are also covered.
food_tips.Local drinks: Calafate sour is the local twist on the pisco sour, made with calafate berry. Both Las Torres and Hotel Lago Grey serve it. Craft beers to look for: Pionera (Las Torres house beer, brewed on site; verified), Austral (a Punta Arenas brewery founded 1896 and now part of CCU; Calafate and Lager varieties; from general knowledge, not checked this session), and Baguales (a Puerto Natales brewpub and brand; from general knowledge, not checked this session). The Grey III ticket includes one pisco sour.
